sub: How a value moves when a model picks its own training data
foot: the loop  ·  two measurements  ·  the one-round rule  ·  the forecast  ·  the limits
narration: A I increasingly generates and selects its own training data. A model's behavior then shapes the data that trains it next. Through that loop, a value it already has can persist, weaken, or amplify. This is the short version of how I measured which one happens.

caption: Six candidates per prompt, a judge keeps two, fine-tune on those two, re-measure on held-out prompts
narration: Each round, the model writes six candidate answers per prompt. A judge keeps two. The model is fine-tuned on those two. Held-out prompts re-measure its value on a zero to one scale. For the gambling organism, the value is the share of answers picking the risky gamble. For the insecure-code organism, it is how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its own coding habits read, scored by its frozen base model.

caption: Spread and agreement, measured inside each prompt's pool and averaged over the round's prompts
narration: Two numbers come out of every round. Spread is the standard deviation of the candidates' value scores within a prompt, averaged over the round's prompts. Agreement is the correlation between the judge's preferences and those same scores, measured the same way.

headline: next value = the mean value score of the two kept candidates
sub: MAE 0.081 across 340 rounds, against 0.128 for assuming no change  ·  every experimental condition held out
narration: The one round rule has no fitted coefficient. Average the value scores of the two candidates the judge kept. That is where the value lands after training on them. Holding out each complete experimental condition in turn, the rule predicts the next measured value far better than assuming no change does.

caption: Spread times agreement predicts the kept-minus-pool gap at R squared 0.80 across 367 rounds
narration: To run the rule forward you need the kept mean before the judge picks. The product of spread and agreement reconstructs the gap between the kept mean and the pool mean closely. Read spread, agreement, and pool composition in round one, hold them fixed, and iterate to the end of the run. Endpoints land at mean absolute error zero point one one eight, against zero point four three one for assuming no change.

caption: Observed above, one simulated draw per run below: 89% of endpoints fall inside the 80% band
narration: That forecast describes the average path that real runs scatter around. Adding the measured noise gives a band instead of a point, and observed endpoints fall inside that band about as often as the model says they should. That is a range, not a number for any one run. The remaining error comes mostly from agreement drifting during a run, because agreement depends on the candidate distribution in front of the judge, and training keeps changing it.

kicker: WHAT THE SETUP DOES NOT COVER
checks: short runs, filtered SFT on a few selected answers
DPO, online RL and constitutional feedback untested
closer: The aim is to know which way a value moves before a model is set loose in its own training loop.
narration: The setup is narrow. Two model families, both small, short runs, and filtered supervised fine-tuning on a few selected answers. Two behaviors, risk preference and insecure-code self-description. Whether the rule holds for larger models, longer runs, other update rules, and wider values is untested. What I want from this work is to understand how a model's values move once it is inside a feedback loop driving its own training, including looser versions of that loop where a model revises its own prompts and edits the loop itself.
